entities.summary:
Martin Schongauer, a renowned Alsatian engraver and painter, was born in the 15th century and died on February 11, 1491. He was the most important printmaker north of the Alps before Albrecht Dürer, a younger artist who collected his work. Schongauer's family background and training in goldsmithing were unusual for early engravers.

Schongauer's contributions to the art world were significant, as he was the first German painter to achieve success as an engraver. His work was collected by prominent artists and patrons, including Dürer, and his engravings are still highly regarded today for their technical skill and artistic merit.

Schongauer's legacy extends beyond his own art, as he helped establish the Alsatian region as a center for artistic innovation. His influence can be seen in the work of later artists, including Dürer and others, who built upon his techniques and artistic vision.

Schongauer's impact on the art world was also marked by his innovative use of techniques, such as the use of aquatint and the creation of intricate designs. His work continues to inspire artists and art historians today, offering a unique glimpse into the artistic traditions of the 15th century.

This masterpiece of Alsatian artistry is a testament to the enduring power of human creativity and innovation, a legacy that continues to inspire and delight audiences around the world.
